name: TRX Atomic Push-Up
description: The TRX atomic push-up combines a push-up with a simultaneous knee tuck, performed with both feet in TRX foot cradles. The push-up phase challenges the chest, triceps, and anterior shoulder; the knee tuck phase challenges the hip flexors and anterior core in compression. The TRX suspension element makes both phases harder by creating instability in multiple planes. This is a highly demanding combined push and core exercise.

execution.starting_position: Place both feet in the TRX foot cradles and assume a push-up plank position with hands on the floor. The TRX straps should be at approximately mid-calf height.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the TRX to a medium height. Begin with the standard TRX push-up and TRX knee tuck separately before combining them.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the push-up plank with both feet in the TRX cradles.
Step 2: Lower the chest to the floor in a controlled push-up.
Step 3: As you press back up, simultaneously drive both knees toward the chest in a knee tuck.
Step 4: Extend both legs back to the plank position. That is one repetition.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale during the push-up descent. Exhale forcefully during the press-up and tuck simultaneously.
common_mistakes: Hips rising during the knee tuck rather than tucking from the core
Doing the push-up and tuck sequentially rather than simultaneously
Losing rigid plank on the return — the body must stay straight as the legs extend back
safety_considerations: This is advanced — master TRX push-up and TRX knee tuck separately before combining
Wrist discomfort may require push-up handles or reduced range
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range combined with a full knee tuck to chest.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3s eccentric push-up, then explosive simultaneous press-up and tuck, then 2s controlled extension back to plank.
coaching_cues: Press up and tuck at the same time — not one then the other
Squeeze the core hard during the tuck — the knees come to the chest, not toward the hands
Control the return — do not let the legs swing back to the plank position
